reading.body:
Google has not published the power capacity, square footage, or building-level details for NBY-7, following its standard disclosure policy of reporting only aggregate figures at the state level. This facility is part of a multi-county Columbus-area campus that received $1.7 billion in announced investment alongside a reported $600 million for the initial New Albany site, placing Google among the largest hyperscale operators in the Licking County corridor alongside AWS and Meta.

Ohio has 76 mapped data center facilities, of which only 8 operators have published power figures totaling 60.4 MW of disclosed capacity across the state. NBY-7 does not contribute to this published total and therefore cannot be ranked against other Ohio facilities by disclosed power.

Without published specifications, NBY-7 cannot be evaluated for its direct relevance to AI scaling in terms of power delivery, rack density, or cooling architecture. The scale of Google's regional investment and its choice to develop in Licking County alongside competing hyperscalers suggests strategic importance to the operator, but individual facility capabilities remain opaque.
